title: LLM 101
summary: A working mental model of how LLMs generate text, why they behave as they do, and how to pick the right model for a task.
outcome: Explain how LLMs work and why they behave as they do, and choose and use the right model for a task.

modules.title: What an LLM Actually Is

topics.d: Generation as a loop of predicting, choosing and appending the next token.
Not a database, search engine, deterministic program or store of canned answers.

topics.t: Why one model does many tasks
topics.d: One model can write, summarize, translate, code, answer and classify.
Better data, more compute, larger models and better training.

modules.tryIt: Run the same prompt several times to see variation, and guess the next word before asking the model.
modules.outcome: Explain simply that an LLM generates text by repeatedly predicting a likely next token.

modules.title: Tokenization

topics.d: Token IDs and why tokenizers split the same text differently.
How English, rare words, numbers, code, emoji and Hindi/Hinglish tokenize.

topics.t: Why tokens drive cost and latency
topics.d: Tokens link to pricing, context usage, latency and spelling/counting errors.

modules.tryIt: Compare token counts for an English paragraph, its Hindi translation, some source code and a list of numbers.
modules.outcome: Explain why texts with similar word counts can differ greatly in tokens and cost.

modules.title: Inside an LLM: Embeddings, Attention & Transformers

topics.d: Tokens become vectors that change across transformer layers.
What sizes like 8B, 70B and 400B+ signify.

topics.t: Why bigger is not automatically better
topics.d: More parameters add capacity but do not guarantee better results.
A token gathers information from relevant tokens in context.
Q, K, V, attention scores and causal masking without the math.
Every parameter participates in every token.
A router activates only a few expert sub-networks per token.
Why a big MoE can be cheaper to run than a dense model of equal total size.
All experts must fit in memory, but per-token compute is smaller.
Interpreting labels like 8x7B and total vs active parameters.

modules.tryIt: Look at an attention visualization for a sentence with an ambiguous pronoun and reason about what the pronoun should attend to.
modules.outcome: Describe what happens between a token entering the model and next-token probabilities coming out.
modules.mentalModel: Text → tokens → embeddings → transformer layers with attention → next-token probabilities

modules.title: How LLMs Learn

topics.d: Next-token prediction on huge corpora supplies its own training signal.
Grammar, facts, patterns, code syntax and problem-solving patterns.
Why a model can answer questions it never saw verbatim.
Pretraining, SFT, preference/RL training, then deployment.
Conceptual view of SFT, RLHF, RLAIF, preference optimization and safety tuning.

topics.t: Why chat models behave as they do
topics.d: Post-training explains instruction following, refusals and hedging.

modules.tryIt: Compare a base model and an instruction-tuned model on identical prompts.
modules.outcome: Explain why a pretrained model may know a lot yet be a poor assistant.

modules.title: How LLM Inference Works

topics.t: What happens after you send a prompt
topics.d: Process input, predict, generate, repeat.
Prefill processes the input; decode generates tokens one at a time.
Input/output tokens, time to first token, tokens per second and total latency.
Caching past attention keys/values so earlier tokens are not recomputed.
Long prompts, long outputs and reasoning models change latency and cost.

modules.outcome: Explain why generating 2,000 output tokens takes far longer than 50, even with the same input.

modules.title: Sampling & Generation Parameters

topics.t: From probabilities to a chosen token
topics.d: Picking the emitted token from the probability distribution.
Greedy decoding, temperature, top-p, top-k, max tokens, stop sequences and penalties.
Low randomness for extraction and QA, higher for brainstorming.
APIs expose different controls; some reasoning models offer few.

modules.tryIt: Run the same prompt at several temperatures and compare consistency, creativity and correctness.
modules.outcome: Choose generation settings deliberately based on the task.

modules.title: Reasoning Models & Test-Time Compute

topics.d: Some models spend much more compute before answering.
Reasoning effort, thinking budgets and internal reasoning tokens.
Hard math, complex code, planning and constraint-heavy problems.
Sentiment, simple extraction, rewriting and plain summaries.
More reasoning can raise quality but usually costs time and money.
State goal, context, constraints and what good looks like rather than step-by-step cues.

modules.tryIt: Run the same problems through a fast general model and a reasoning model and compare accuracy, latency and cost.
modules.outcome: Recognize when extra reasoning compute is worth paying for.

modules.title: The Context Window

topics.d: Instructions, history, documents, examples, tool outputs and generated text.
What is in context vs what the model learned vs long-term memory.

topics.t: What goes wrong in long contexts
topics.d: Truncation, attention dilution and lost-in-the-middle effects.

topics.t: Why a big window is not enough
topics.d: A large window does not mean every token is used equally well.

modules.tryIt: Place a key fact at the start, middle and end of a long document and compare how well it is retrieved.
modules.outcome: Decide whether a task needs a bigger window or better selection of what goes in.

modules.title: LLM Capabilities & Failure Modes

topics.d: Summarizing, transforming, extracting, classifying, coding, translating and few-shot adaptation.
Hallucination, arithmetic slips, brittle reasoning, prompt sensitivity, stale knowledge and confident errors.
Models produce likely continuations without verifying claims.
Judge performance under your application's real conditions.

modules.tryIt: Write 10 questions covering known, unknown, misleading and under-specified cases, and observe how confident the model is.
modules.outcome: Predict which tasks suit LLMs and which need extra safeguards.

modules.title: Understanding the Model Landscape

topics.d: Frontier capability and convenience vs privacy, vendor dependence and control.
Self-hosting, customization and the operational burden that comes with it.
Cloud platforms serving models in your account and providers hosting open weights.
Small vs large, dense vs MoE, reasoning vs not, text-only vs multimodal.

topics.t: There is no universally best LLM
topics.d: The best model depends on the workload.
New information must come through context, retrieval or tools.
Pin versions and re-test when models change or retire.
Permissive, restricted and non-commercial licenses differ in what you can ship.

modules.outcome: Compare two models on architecture, capability and deployment, not leaderboard rank alone.

modules.title: Benchmarks & Leaderboards

topics.d: A fixed task set and scoring method for comparing models.
Knowledge, reasoning, coding and math tests such as MMLU and GPQA.
Human-preference rankings, capability/cost dashboards and open-model boards.
Different prompts, tasks and definitions of 'good' limit transfer to your app.
Contamination, saturation, overfitting to public tests and favorable settings.
Use benchmarks to narrow the field, then test on your own examples.

modules.tryIt: Shortlist three leaderboard models for a task, then compare published scores with results on ten of your own examples.
modules.outcome: Read benchmarks critically and turn them into a shortlist, not a decision.

modules.title: Choosing the Right Model

topics.d: The criteria used to evaluate candidate models.
Can the model do the task at all?
How reliably does it do your specific task?
How quickly does it respond?
What each request costs at expected volume.
Can it accept the input you need to send?
Text, images, audio or video needs.
Public API, managed platform or self-hosted.
Structured outputs, tool calling, streaming and caching.
Critically reading cards, pricing, context specs and API docs.

topics.t: Why benchmarks alone are not enough
topics.d: Benchmarks should not decide model selection by themselves.
Define task, list requirements, shortlist, test, measure, inspect failures, choose.

modules.outcome: Select models from application requirements and measured performance, not popularity.
